card.job: Show and hide sections of text so a long page stays short.

Secondary detail should stay one click away without leaving the page.
One piece of optional detail sits inline in a sentence or a card: use the disclosure form.

One metric with a hidden breakdown, such as credits remaining.
A table row has detail that belongs to that row.
The content is a short list of actions or choices.

card.job: Lay out a whole agent screen: past sessions, the thread and a docked composer.
card.purpose: The page layout for an AI agent. A session list sits in a side column, the thread scrolls in the middle at reading measure, and the composer docks at the bottom with the thread fading under it. With data-fill it takes the viewport height under the top bar. Below 760px the side column leaves and the thread takes the width.
useWhen: The product is a conversation with an agent and the screen is the agent: ask, watch it work, read the answer.
People return to earlier runs and need the session list beside the thread.

avoidWhen.when: The conversation is help or support inside another product screen.
One endpoint with options is tried through a request form and a response panel.
A page needs only a prompt box, not the whole screen.

card.job: Mark a launch or milestone with one full-width accent panel.
card.purpose: An accent surface for a launch or milestone at the top of an overview, with an ASCII flame field on each side and the message in the clear middle. It is the one place a whole surface may be accent. Under 640px the end art drops away and the start art becomes a band across the top.

A product overview opens with one statement and one or two actions.

avoidWhen.when: The message is one line about the account, such as a trial ending.
The message belongs to a section and needs a tone.
A short, fleeting confirmation after an action.
Several announcements compete on the page.

The art on the trailing edge; it is dropped under 640px.

card.job: Frame every signed-in screen with a sidebar, a top bar and a page.

A docs site with its own two-row top bar and contents column.

Parts of a total where order matters more than proportion.

card.job: Sign a surface with the product mark and name, an uploaded logo or a wordmark.

A product sets its brand once, as JSON in a data-fd-brand script or with setBrand(), and every fd-brand on the page is filled from it: the name, a picture mark or the initial of the name, a logo with a dark variant, the link.

A page says "Powered by" with a small wordmark.
A product white-labels itself: one record of name, mark and logo fills the sidebar, the top bar, the auth screens and the docs bar.

card.job: See how values change over time or between periods.
card.purpose: An SVG line, area, bar or stacked bar chart from a JSON config: labels, up to six series, an optional threshold. Hairline grid, mono axes, the first series in the accent. card.job: Group the fields of a long form under a title.
card.purpose: One titled group in a long create or edit form: a narrow head with a title and one line on the left (it stays in view while the body scrolls) and the fields on a white surface beside it. Below about 720px of form width the head stacks above the body. Use it inside a form with data-size="full".

People should scan titles and skip what they do not need.

card.job: Lay out equal columns that fill the width and reflow.
card.purpose: An auto-filling grid. data-min sets the narrowest column (a size token from 4xs to 6xl, or full), data-cols the most columns, and data-span on a child covers several columns (or full). It drops columns on narrow screens by itself, so markup never sets a width.

One child needs to span several columns (data-span).

Children are a list of cards that wrap with their own sizes.

avoidWhen.when: A form has columns of fields.

card.job: Let one child take the space left over in a row.
card.purpose: A flex-grow helper: put it on the child of a row or stack that should absorb the remaining space, pushing its siblings to the ends. On an fd-divider it makes a rule that fills the row.

A rule must fill the space on either side of an "or".

avoidWhen.when: Children should spread evenly.
Children are equal columns.
A band must fill the height of a centred screen.

parts.role: The class on the child that grows.

card.job: See activity over weeks, one cell per day, or an outcome per day.
card.purpose: A grid of day cells: weeks run in columns, Monday to Sunday in rows. Five steps run from a faint ink wash to the full accent, cut at the quartiles of the busy days so one spike does not flatten the rest. The strip variant shows one row of days with a tone each and a legend, for pass, slow or fail.

Each day has an outcome, not an amount: use the strip with a legend.
A table cell needs the last 14 days at a glance: strip at data-size="sm".

A single day or week.
One quantity against a limit.
Exact numbers for each day.

The strongest level.

card.job: Wait a few seconds before an action goes, with a countdown and Undo.
card.purpose: A strip with a ring that drains with the time left, the action in words, a note that nothing has happened yet, and Undo. A commit with data-fd-hold or a button with data-fd-hold-for starts it; focus moves to Undo. Undo or Escape stops it and returns focus; the end fires fd:commit. Leaving the page sends it. Screen readers hear the start and the undo. toast.hold draws the same ring in a toast.
useWhen: Sending is hard to take back: money, access, a message, a shipped change, a cancelled run.
A person commits in one press and deserves a moment to change their mind.

avoidWhen.when: It is already done and the server can reverse it.
A mistake destroys history and must not happen by one press.
Work that runs for minutes with progress to watch.

states.name: running
states.how: data-state="running" while it counts; the trigger is disabled

states.name: idle
states.how: hidden until a hold starts, and again once it is undone or sent

variants.useWhen: The held action removes or stops something; a danger commit button sets it.
The length of a hold started by data-fd-hold-for; 10 by default, 5 inside a dialog.

parts.role: The countdown ring; data-size="sm" in a toast.
The whole seconds left, inside the ring.
The action in progress: "Approving the credit".

keyboard.does: Stops the hold when focus is in it, in its form, or nowhere.
On Undo: stops the hold and returns focus to the button that started it.

card.job: Preview a link's target, such as a person or a provider, without leaving the page.
card.purpose: A card that opens after half a second of hovering a link, stays open while the pointer travels into it, and closes a quarter second after leaving. It holds a title, meta, a line of text and a few stats. It is not for actions or forms.

Preview facts are read-only: a role, counts, a date.

avoidWhen.when: The content has actions, inputs or links people must click.
Naming an icon button or a shortcut.
The preview is needed on touch devices.
A short list of choices.

states.name: open
states.how: data-state="open"; opens 500ms after hover, set by data-open-delay

states.name: closing
states.how: data-state="closing" for a quarter second after leaving

parts.role: A muted line, such as an email and role.

keyboard.does: Focusing the link opens the card.
Closes the card.

card.job: Draw a small symbol beside a label or on a button.
card.purpose: A 16px line icon from Fire's sprite, written as <i data-icon="name"> and drawn once at start (or as the fd-icon element with icon="name"). Sizes are 12, 14, 16, 20, 24 or 32 (plus sm and lg); tone sets its colour. It is decorative: name the control that holds it with a label. Change it with setIcon(el, name).

An empty state or a tile needs one glyph.

avoidWhen.when: The symbol is the only content and no label exists.
avoidWhen.instead: Add an aria-label or data-fd-tooltip to the control that holds it.

avoidWhen.when: A person's image is needed.
A brand mark is needed.
A tile with a coloured background holds the glyph.

states.name: filled
states.how: data-icon-fill on icons that have a filled form

variants.useWhen: Inside a dense chip or a badge.
Beside small text.
The default beside body text and in buttons.
A larger toolbar or a list row.
A prominent control or an empty state.
A hero or a large empty state.
The icon marks the brand colour.
An arrow that moves a little on hover, for an external link.

card.job: Say how much a change will touch, before anyone commits it.
card.purpose: A tinted block that leads with a count in figures ("29 teams change"), one line on how they change, a short list of the largest with their before and after values, and "and 26 more" with a link to all. data-tone warns when the reach is wide. It is the result of a preview, or part of a case whose change reaches beyond one record.
useWhen: A change reaches more than the one thing on screen: a plan default, a crawl setting, a policy.
A preview must show its reach before the commit button appears.

avoidWhen.when: The change touches one record, which the brief already names.
A warning with no figure and no list.
Figures to read without a decision.

variants.useWhen: The reach is wide or the change is hard to take back.
The change removes access or data for those it touches.
A neutral reach worth knowing, such as a default for new teams only.

parts.role: The figure in bold and what it counts.
One line on how they change.
A few of them, each with an fd-delta or a figure.
How many more, and a link to the full list.

card.job: Show an organisation's first letter as a dot-matrix mark where it has no logo.
card.purpose: A drawn mark: the first letter of a name on a 5 by 7 grid of dots, lit dots in the box's colour and unlit ones faint. The same name always draws the same glyph and takes the same tone. It goes in a brand mark, tile or avatar through data-fd-initial, or as an SVG string from initial.js on a server or in an email.
useWhen: An organisation, team or brand has no uploaded logo and needs a mark in the brand slot, a tile or an avatar.
An email or a server-rendered page needs the same mark: call initialMark() or initialRows(), no DOM needed.
A list of organisations should be told apart at a glance without anyone choosing a colour.

avoidWhen.when: A person's initials, or a box smaller than 28px.
The thing has a real logo or a symbol: an icon, an image.
The product's own mark, or a logotype in the current colour.

states.name: no script
states.how: the host keeps its own letter, styled by the tile or avatar

states.name: other character

parts.role: The drawing: an svg in currentColor, sized by its box.

card.job: Mark a command, a path or a key inside a sentence.
card.purpose: Inline code in the mono face on a faint fill (fd-code), with a tone for status words, and a keyboard key cap (fd-kbd). Use it for identifiers, flags, file names and shortcuts that a person might copy or press, never for emphasis.
useWhen: A sentence names a file, a flag, an endpoint or a value.
A shortcut is shown as a key cap (fd-kbd), as in a search hint.

avoidWhen.when: The code is several lines or needs copying.
A command is shown to run.
The words are emphasis.
A status is shown.

variants.useWhen: A code span in the accent colour.

card.job: Type one line of text, a URL, a key or a number.
card.purpose: The native input in Fire's field skin: a white surface, a 1px line drawn inside the box so nothing shifts between states, 36px tall. Hover darkens the line, focus swaps it for the accent and adds a halo, aria-invalid turns it danger. It also works as a span in the same shape to show a value people read but do not edit.

People paste or compare characters, so a mono face helps (data-mono): keys, paths, regular expressions.
A read-only value must line up with real inputs (a span with the same class).

avoidWhen.when: The value is a number people nudge up or down.
The value is a long answer over several lines.
The value is one of a fixed set.
The value is a secret or a new password.
A prefix, unit or button sits inside the field.
The value is a list of URLs, domains or emails.

states.how: disabled

A short value such as a port or a code; the width follows the size attribute.

A field and a button side by side; stacks on phones.

card.job: Put an icon, prefix, unit or button inside one field.
card.purpose: One field with affixes: the group carries the single hairline and focus halo, and a bare fd-input lives inside it. Affixes are an icon, a text prefix, a unit, a chevron or a small ghost button one step below the field size. The same group holds the input of a combobox.

A button belongs to the value inside the field: copy, show, apply.
An icon or a chevron marks what the field is.

The field is a search with a clear button.
The value is a number with steppers.
The field picks from a list.

states.name: entry

A unit in mono after a number: ms, MB, requests.

A chevron that opens a list; used by the combobox.

A larger field.
A short value; the width follows the input's size attribute.

card.job: Explore a JSON response by folding it, not by reading it whole.

A toolbar adds a label, size, Expand all, Collapse all and Copy.

People need the path to a nested value.
A result offers a Table | JSON switch of the same data.

Records with the same fields.
Parameter docs.
A diff between two JSON documents.

card.job: Read what an object is as labelled values in a grid.

Hairlines between rows of a split list.

The value is an ID, a path or a hash.
The value is a sentence, not an identifier.
Keys in normal text instead of mono capitals.

card.purpose: A row of small swatches and muted labels. A single series.

A line swatch with a faded fill for areas.
A series that means failure.

An inbox where unread rows carry a dot.

card.purpose: Two panes: a list of rows (buttons with data-value) and the record that is open. The open row has aria-current="true" and the accent wash. The list must stay in view while one record is open, and a phone shows the list first.

avoidWhen.when: Each record needs its own page and address.
The side pane is settings navigation.
The detail is a short summary over the page.

states.how: data-view="detail": below 760px only the record shows, with fd-list-detail-back

The rows are checkboxes or radios in a form.

card.job: Show that something small is loading with a ring, dots, bars or a text frame.

A stream is receiving data and needs a quiet live mark.
A change shows at once at half strength and settles when the server confirms.

A page or a region whose layout is known; sketch it.
Navigation or a full reload.
A button is busy; set aria-busy="true" on it instead of adding a spinner child.
Progress with a known amount.

Live work the person is waiting on.
A quiet spinner that should not draw the eye.

A CLI session is shown as a terminal.
People link to a line of a finished log, or need to land on the first error.

The history of one thing in events.
Records with columns.
A summary of what happened.

elements.description:
A Fire chart drawn from data given as a property: line, area, bar and stacked charts, quadrants, sparklines, donuts and
progress rings, heat grids and strips. The element is the chart's root: it carries the root class of its type
(`fd-chart` for the cartesian types and the quadrant, `fd-sparkline`, `fd-donut` or `fd-heatgrid`) and the markup form's data-* attributes, holds the data
as the markup form's `<script type="application/json">`, and Fire's charts module draws the chart inside it, so it
looks and behaves exactly like the markup form. Setting `data` (or any attribute) redraws it, without the entrance
animation. Changing `type` to another kind of chart (say from `line` to `donut`) is not supported: render a new
element (in React or Vue, give it a new `key`).

Attributes mirror the markup form's `data-*` attributes; each applies to the types named. A function in the data
(a custom `yFormat`) is kept for cartesian charts, which are drawn from the object itself; the other types are
drawn from the JSON, so their formats are names.

elements.description:
A Fire code block that highlights the text it is given. The element is the block's root: it carries
`class="fd-codeblock"` and the markup form's data-* attributes, renders the block's internals (an optional header
or copy button, then `<pre class="fd-codeblock-body"><code data-lang="…">`), puts `code` in it as text and lets
Fire's code module tokenise it into lines, so it looks and behaves exactly like the markup form. Unlike the markup
form inside a framework, Fire never rewrites text nodes the framework owns: changing `code` (or any attribute)
renders the internals afresh.

Languages: `json`, `bash`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `python` and their aliases (`sh`, `curl`, `js`, `ts`, `py`, …);
any other name shows plain text.

elements.description:
One of Fire's icons (a Lucide subset). The element is the icon's root, as `svg.fd-icon` is for the markup form:
it carries `class="fd-icon"`, `data-icon`, `data-size` and `aria-hidden="true"`, so every `.fd-icon` rule applies
to it, direct-child rules such as `.fd-btn > .fd-icon` included. Inside it, an SVG drawn from Fire's sprite fills
it (fire/base.css). Use it in framework code, where an `<i data-icon>` that replaces itself would break the
framework's reconciliation. The icon is decorative: name the control that holds it.

An unknown name draws nothing and logs a warning, as the markup form does.

elements.description:
A Fire generative field: terrain, waves, orbit, rain, grid, flame, halftone, spark, contour, stipple or bars, drawn in characters, dots, squares, plus signs or dashes. The element is
the field's root: it carries the markup form's `class="fd-ascii"`, `data-fd-ascii="…"`,
the other `data-*` attributes and `aria-hidden="true"`, and Fire's texture module draws its canvas inside it and owns
its size, colour and animation (12 fps on a shared frame loop, paused off screen, one still frame under reduced
motion). Being the field keeps Fire's layering rule, which puts a field between its container's background and its
content, working as it does for the markup form. Changing a property re-reads the settings and redraws.

The field fills its nearest positioned ancestor, or flows at the field height with `inline`. It is decorative.

attributes.description: The field: `terrain`, `waves`, `orbit`, `rain`, `grid`, `flame`, `halftone`, `spark`, `contour`, `stipple`, `bars` or a registered name (`data-fd-ascii`). A page signature field, when set, wins over it unless `signature` is `own`; left out, it is that field, else `terrain`.

attributes.name: ramp
attributes.description: Character ramp: `default`, `soft`, `dense`, `glyph`, `rain`, or a literal ramp such as ` .:-=+*#` (`data-ramp`).

attributes.name: speed

attributes.name: tone
